reference_action: Fungal leaf spots; OP reports recovery after a commercial fungicide every two weeks per label. Switching from kitchen vinegar to a plant fungicide is the validated action; pruning alone was suggested but not credited with recovery.

sources.reason: For spreading spots without pests, consider systemic fungicide; matches the commercial-fungicide action, without copper or label details.
Explicit copper fungicide per label on both leaf surfaces matches the validated treatment; static article used, not its promoted AI diagnosis service.
Watering, root rot, nutrition and humidity advice; no fungal leaf-spot fungicide treatment.
Pruning diseased leaves and monitoring only; OP specifically credits repeated fungicide, not pruning alone.
Explicit indoor-safe copper fungicide for fungal spots recovers the treatment, alongside pruning and airflow advice.

actions.action: Inspect spot texture, soil moisture, recent changes and pests
Unpot and inspect roots if wet spots or musty soil
Trim damaged roots if rot found
Repot in well-draining mix and root-sized pot
Water when top two to four inches dry
Add humidifier if humidity below forty percent
Move to indirect light or install sheer curtain
Wipe pests with alcohol swab or spray neem
Trim extensively damaged leaves with clean shears

resolved.reason: Fungal disease and a fungicide appear in the relevant pest-free spreading-spot branch. The treatment is merely an option among many diagnoses, with no product, label or interval guidance; several overconfident pattern rules conflict with diagnostic uncertainty.

harmfulness.reason: “If pests present” and root inspection before cutting are useful safeguards. “Consider systemic fungicide” omits label-use guidance, and overly categorical pattern rules could send the user toward unnecessary root surgery despite the nursery finding no rot.

specificity_accuracy.reason: The no-visible-pests fungal branch matches the history and includes the successful treatment class. The unsupported percentages and claim that wet soil confirms overwatering exaggerate diagnostic certainty, and the answer never addresses vinegar directly.

feasibility.reason: Soil checks, isolation and moving the plant are practical. The many conditional actions, humidifier purchase and unspecified fungicide or neem application make the full regimen less executable.
